reviewer: Codex merchant owner; personally inspected fresh surface-renewal images

views.name: hull_rig
findings: Separate square canvas tiers, stays and ratlines remain readable around the three masts; the aft fore-and-aft canvas and its long yard are visible.
The ochre planked hull, green stern, small glazed lights, projecting gun muzzles and external rudder remain distinct in the whole-ship view.
views.scope: Whole actual GLB with all visible hull, rig and sails.

views.name: deck_closeup
findings: The coamed hatch exposes a complete stair with individual treads, timber side rails and rope handholds; the opening shows actual structure below the deck.
Lengthwise grain, staggered plank joints, capstan whelps and messenger turns remain clear. Cropped cannon portions shade as dark curved metal; most of each gun lies outside this hatch-focused frame.
views.scope: Actual deck and fitting close-up at a fixed 4.5 metre physical field; rig hidden for visibility.

views.name: hold_interior
findings: Curved hull-side frames, knees and repeated overhead beams define a fully framed hold beneath the planked ceiling; the structure is much more articulated than the old Brig hold.
The grained sole has distinct plank seams and a clear passage beside the foreground mast and lantern-topped crate. The far casks and opposite-side bays remain in shadow.
views.scope: Camera inside the actual enclosed GLB room; auxiliary camera fill reveals timber and furniture.

views.name: hold_cutaway
findings: The removed outer skin and upper slabs expose the hold sole, paired curved frames, separate access stairs, cargo casks and crates across the vessel length.
The weatherdeck cannon rows and their carriages remain above the framing. Hidden supporting layers make some fittings appear suspended; this is an explicitly temporary structural cutaway.
views.scope: Read-only cutaway: named outer hull, upper deck timbers and bulkheads temporarily hidden; delivered GLB unchanged.

views.name: cabin_interior
findings: Grained sole planks, ceiling boards and overhead timbers enclose the cabin. The central mast and its partner partly obstruct the actual framed doorway behind it.

A chart table, bench and ring-handled lantern occupy the left side; a strapped chest and white-topped berth occupy the right. The visible floor stays clear, while part of the berth lies outside the frame.
views.scope: Camera inside the actual enclosed GLB room; auxiliary camera fill reveals timber and furniture.

views.name: cabin_cutaway
findings: The temporary cutaway exposes the white-topped berth, chart desk, seating and open-lid close-stool with its actual dark seat opening, framed floor and stern lights.

The nearby full cannon body shades smoothly around its circumference with distinct profile rings; the regular rectangular facet breakup is absent. Mottled patina and pronounced reflections remain visible.
views.scope: Read-only cutaway: named outer hull, upper deck timbers and bulkheads temporarily hidden; delivered GLB unchanged.

limitations: The intact hold has a dark far bay; the central cabin mast partly obscures the doorway and part of the berth lies outside that frame.
Cutaways temporarily hide declared structural layers and can expose apparently suspended hardware.
Existing iron patina and reflections remain stylized; static imagery does not certify gameplay controls or exact historical identity.
instructions: Inspect every listed actual image and the matched old Brig reference views. Add at least two concrete observations per view. Set decision PASS only after inspection. A cutaway remains supplementary to the separate intact interior view.
